title: Migrant domestic worker hiring costs and protections
asked: Dr Choo Pei Ling asked whether the Ministry of Manpower plans to further reduce upfront hiring costs for migrant domestic workers for families with young children or vulnerable elderly, and to enhance protections against agency misrepresentation and against MDWs who commit offences or leave for reasons not due to employer fault, such as homesickness.
response: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong said the median upfront recruitment outlay is around $4,700, about half of which is a loan to the MDW that the employer recovers, and has been largely stable since 2022 after inflation. He said more than 2,500 licensed employment agencies compete on price, and MOM's online EA directory lets employers compare track record; EAs must refund at least 50% of service fees if a contract ends within six months without a suitable replacement. Families with young children and elderly get concessionary levies of about $60 a month instead of $300, saving about $5,760 over two years. MDWs who commit serious offences are barred from future employment, and employers can use the FDW e-service portal to check past work performance and reasons for leaving.

key_points.point: The median upfront recruitment outlay to hire a new MDW is around $4,700, about half of which is a loan to the MDW that the employer recovers.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: The median upfront recruitment outlay to hire new migrant domestic workers (MDW) is around $4,700, of which half consists of loan to the MDWs that the employer subsequently recovers.

key_points.point: This upfront cost has been largely stable since 2022 after accounting for inflation.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: This upfront cost has remained largely stable since 2022, after accounting for inflation.

key_points.point: More than 2,500 employment agencies are licensed to place MDWs, and they must consider market competition when pricing services.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: With more than 2,500 employment agencies (EAs) licenced to place MDWs, EAs have to take into account market competition when they are pricing their services.

key_points.point: MOM's online EA directory lets employers compare EAs' track record, including customer service ratings, years of service, and retention and transfer rates.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: We provide information on Ministry of Manpower's (MOM's) online EA directory to enable employers to compare EAs' track record such as customer service ratings, years of service, and retention and transfer rate of MDWs when choosing EAs.

key_points.point: If an MDW's contract is terminated within the first six months without a suitable replacement, MOM requires EAs to refund at least 50% of service fees.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: MOM requires EAs to refund employers at least 50% of the service fees paid if MDW's contract is terminated within the first six months of employment without a suitable replacement.

key_points.point: Families with young children and elderly get concessionary levies of about $60 a month instead of $300.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: Families with young children and elderly enjoy significant subsidies today in the form of concessionary levies at about $60 a month instead of $300.

key_points.point: This amounts to about $5,760 in savings over two years.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: This amounts to about $5,760 in savings over two years.

key_points.point: MDWs who commit serious offences, such as stealing, are barred from future employment in Singapore.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: MDWs who commit serious offences, such as stealing, are barred from future employment in Singapore.

key_points.point: Prospective employers can use the FDW e-service portal to check an MDW's past work performance, length of each employment, and reasons for leaving.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: Prospective employers may use the FDW e-service portal to assess information about MDWs' past work performance, length of each employment and reasons why these MDWs left their past employment before hiring.

key_points.point: Agency service fees are generally left to market forces.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: We generally allow agency service fees to be determined by market forces.

key_points.point: There are already fee caps on EAs for the amount they can charge MDWs.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: there are already fee caps on EAs, the amount that they can charge the MDWs

key_points.point: The Caregiving Grant provides about $400 and will increase to $600 in April 2026.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: the Caregiving Grant, which provides about $400 of payout, and this will be increased in April 2026 to $600.

key_points.point: Families without caregiving needs can consider part-time cleaning under the Household Services Scheme.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: For families without caregiving needs, they also can consider part time cleaning services under the Household Services Scheme, which may be more affordable.

left_open: Whether there are plans to further reduce upfront recruitment costs for families with young children or vulnerable elderly.
Whether there are plans to enhance protections against misrepresentation from agencies.
How cases where MDWs wish to cease work for reasons not due to employer fault, such as homesickness, are handled.
supplementary: Supplementary question asked whether benchmark ranges for agency fees should be set to prevent excessive charges and ensure affordability.
